datasets: NIBRS Group A Crime Data (Open Baltimore)
concurrency_primitives: Per-file streaming reader goroutine -> batches channel (cap workers*2) -> N parser goroutines with private slices/interners -> results channel, WaitGroup (internal/ingest/csv.go:117-205); 3 files loaded concurrently (pipeline.go:118-134); generic fold fan-out/fan-in with private accumulators for index and join, 3 dataset folds in parallel (pipeline.go:166-246); 5 analyses in 5 goroutines writing own result slots (analysis.go:36-49)
design_patterns: Pipeline (4 explicit stages), Builder (pipeline.NewBuilder().Crime().Requests().Licenses().Workers().Window().Build()), Strategy (analysis.Analysis interface, 5 implementations), Factory (report.New("terminal"|"html") Renderer); generics for Load[T] and fold[T,A]
questions: Which 311 request types track violent crime across neighborhoods after adjusting for total 311 volume?
Do neighborhoods with more active liquor licenses see more night-time (21:00-03:59) violent crime?
Do high-crime neighborhoods wait longer for 311 requests to be closed?
Are street blocks with a liquor license more violent than blocks without one, and which license types stand out?
Which neighborhoods need combined intervention first (weighted priority index over violent crime, 311 demand, slow response, license density)?
stakeholders: Department of Public Works / Department of Transportation
Board of Liquor License Commissioners / Baltimore Police Department
City Planning / Board of Liquor License Commissioners
overview: Professional multi-package Go (internal/model, geo, ingest, pipeline, analysis, report, stats) with a streaming worker-pool CSV loader, a generic fan-out/fan-in fold, a normalized street-block join key with a majority-vote block-to-neighborhood index, Builder/Strategy/Factory patterns that actually exist in code, deterministic output, and 15 passing tests including an end-to-end run on real data slices. Highly maintainable; README, code and runtime behavior are fully consistent.
stakeholder_value: Each question names its stakeholder and joins at least two datasets (Q4 and Q5 use all three at block level). Q3 refutes an equity hypothesis with data, Q4's 5.7x licensed-block finding and Q5's transparent weighted priority index are directly usable by Planning and the Mayor's Office. Q1's headline correlate is a noisy low-volume request type, though the dirty-street/illegal-dumping signals below it are meaningful.
issues: Q1 headline picks a low-volume oddly specific 311 type (HLTH-Animal ... Standby) as the top size-adjusted correlate
Q4 unlicensed-block baseline is biased upward because event-free blocks are absent from the data (acknowledged in report)
run.sh builds into bin/ inside the project folder
rationale: Every rubric criterion is met with verified evidence: clean build and vet, three large real bundled Open Baltimore datasets, parallel parse and parallel join/aggregate that pass the race detector on the full 458 MB input, documented and measured memory management, realized design patterns in a clean package layout with tests, and five cross-dataset questions for named stakeholders with ASCII and HTML charts. One point withheld for a noisy Q1 headline. Total 99, A.
